blueprint_concepts: Integral part and fractional part of (a + sqrt(b))^n
english: Let $[t]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. Then the value of $\left[\left(1-\sqrt{2}\right)^{-7}\right]$ is ______.
hindi: माना $[t]$, $t$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है। तब $\left[\left(1-\sqrt{2}\right)^{-7}\right]$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: In $(1+\sqrt{2})^{7}+(1-\sqrt{2})^{7}$ the odd powers of $\sqrt{2}$ cancel and the even ones double: $2\left[\binom{7}{0}+\binom{7}{2}(\sqrt{2})^{2}+\binom{7}{4}(\sqrt{2})^{4}+\binom{7}{6}(\sqrt{2})^{6}\right]=2(1+42+140+56)=478$.
Hence $(1+\sqrt{2})^{7}=478+(\sqrt{2}-1)^{7}$, a number slightly larger than $478$ (about $478.0021$).
Therefore $(1-\sqrt{2})^{-7}=-478-(\sqrt{2}-1)^{7}$, which lies strictly between $-479$ and $-478$, and its greatest integer is $-479$.
(Taking the integer part of $(1+\sqrt{2})^{7}$ and only changing the sign would give $-478$, which is wrong for a negative non-integer.)
originality_note: New: a negative power of 1 - sqrt2 that is minus (1 + sqrt2)^7, so the integral-part argument must be done for a negative number (way 4, hidden reciprocal). Closest known: integral part of (2 + sqrt3)^n or (1 + sqrt2)^n. Different because: the reciprocal relation and the negative greatest-integer value are the traps.

concept_use.Integral part and fractional part of (a: (1+sqrt2)^7 = 478 + (sqrt2 - 1)^7 gives its integral part and fractional part, and then the greatest integer of the negative number.

stem_review: Read as a student: [t] defined as greatest integer (not truncation), so the negative value floors to -479; answer -479 is a negative integer as planned; checked numerically -478.0021; Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: Use (1 - sqrt2)^(-1) = -(1 + sqrt2) and the conjugate sum 478.
justification: Standard conjugate-pair argument with one extra step (reciprocal) and a sign trap; routine chain. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q4 (L2, a range-shift trap).
